config.title: Berlin Botanic Garden - FAQ
config.subtitle: Practical answers on whether the Dahlem garden fits your Berlin day, what to prioritise and what to check live before travel.

items.q: Is Berlin Botanic Garden worth the trip from Mitte?
items.a: Yes if you want a slower half-day with glasshouses, outdoor paths and space to look properly. It is less useful on a single rushed first day when you still need the historic centre, Wall history and the essential sights.

items.q: What should I see first at Berlin Botanic Garden?
items.a: If the weather is uncertain or time is short, start with the Great Tropical House and choose one outdoor section afterwards. On a dry day with more time, walk outside first and let a glasshouse be the calmer finish.

items.q: How much time should I allow for Berlin Botanic Garden?
items.a: About 90 minutes works for one glasshouse anchor plus one outdoor contrast. A calm half-day is better if you want the outdoor garden to matter. Trying to cover every collection in a short visit usually makes the place feel like a checklist.

items.q: How much are tickets for Berlin Botanic Garden?
items.a: The official ticket page listed adult admission at €10 and reduced admission at €5 when this guide was checked. Prices and conditions can change, so confirm the live page before travel and buy online when the Garden recommends it for queues.

items.q: Is the Botanical Museum open with the garden?
items.a: No. The Garden's current visitor information says the Botanical Museum exhibition areas are closed for modernisation until approximately 2027. Plan the visit around the outdoor garden and glasshouses instead.
